goal: Lets IPC mining clients (like Stratum v2 template providers) see how much memory the node is holding for block-template transactions outside the mempool.
Solves the problem that IPC clients can hold block templates indefinitely, pinning transaction memory that would otherwise be freed.
reviewability: Ready to review, though it is stacked on the still-open block-template-manager PR #35675 and the diff mixes that base work with this PR's own commits.
Review #35675 first for the shared plumbing, then focus on the four commits unique to this PR.
agreement: Concept ACKs from ryanofsky and ismaelsadeeq, full ACKs from vasild and enirox001, though those ACKs predate a later design switch to build on #35675 (ryanofsky, ismaelsadeeq, vasild, enirox001).

ismaelsadeeq argued client-managed memory release is the wrong model and proposed internal FIFO eviction instead, author disagreed and no resolution was reached but neither side blocks (ismaelsadeeq, Sjors).
A mutation-testing pass found a real reference-counting bug in the destructor logic, which was fixed and covered by an added test (brunoerg).

result.summary: Adds a getMemoryLoad() IPC method and internal bookkeeping (TxTemplateMap) so the node can report the memory footprint of transactions that are still referenced by outstanding block templates but no longer in the mempool. No limit is enforced; this is purely visibility/monitoring. The PR sits on top of the open #35675 block template manager PR and shares much of its plumbing, with only the last four commits (hasher refactor, memory tracking, GetTemplateMemoryUsage, getMemoryLoad) being unique to this PR. It has been rebased dozens of times as dependency PRs merged and as the author switched underlying designs.
result.problem: IPC clients (e.g. Stratum v2 template providers via sv2-tp) can hold references to block templates indefinitely, and each held template pins the transactions it references outside the mempool, growing memory in a way the node cannot currently observe or account for. This is a real but currently small operational risk for external mining software built on the multiprocess mining interface.

open_concerns: ismaelsadeeq's concept objection that memory management should be handled internally via FIFO eviction rather than delegated to well-behaved clients remains unresolved, though non-blocking (agree to disagree).
The PR is stacked on #35675, itself open, so final shape may still shift.
resolved_concerns: Thread-safety gap in the shared map identified by ryanofsky, fixed by adding a mutex.
Mutation-testing-found reference-count bug in ~BlockTemplateImpl fixed and covered by an expanded test (brunoerg).
Naming and wording nits from vasild addressed.
Hash-flooding DoS concern about CTransactionRef hashing resolved by switching to a salted hasher (vasild, maflcko).

result.card: This PR adds a getMemoryLoad() IPC method and internal tracking (TxTemplateMap) so Bitcoin Core can report how much memory is consumed by transactions that block templates reference outside the mempool, addressing the risk that IPC clients (e.g. Stratum v2 template providers) can hold templates indefinitely and pin transaction memory. The author measured the real-world footprint as minuscule on mainnet so far, but the mechanism unblocks safer external use of the multiprocess mining interface (a consumer PR already exists in stratum-mining/sv2-tp#63). It is draft and stacked on the still-open #35675 (block template manager), sharing much of that PR's plumbing; only four commits are unique to this PR. Review is substantively positive (concept ACKs from ryanofsky and ismaelsadeeq, full ACKs from vasild and enirox001) but those ACKs predate a July 2026 rebase onto the new base, and ismaelsadeeq's objection that memory management should be handled internally via FIFO eviction rather than delegated to clients was never resolved, just left as a non-blocking disagreement. A mutation-testing pass caught and fixed a real reference-counting bug in the template destructor, and the salted-hash design for CTransactionRef was hardened against hash-flooding after discussion with vasild and maflcko.
